High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Manoj Jain, learned counsel for the respondent N  ORDER 1.
This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellant(s) assailing the impugned award dated 19.9.2023 passed by 1st Addl.
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Sardarpur, District Dhar (M.P.)

in Claim Case No.74/2021 whereby an amount of 11,71,000/- along with interest has been awarded to the survivors of the deceased Smt. Kala Bai,
who passed away in road traffic accident which occurred on 24.11.2020 involving the offending vehicle bearing registration No.M.P. 11 MZ 6769.
2.
Facts of the case are that on 24.11.2020 deceased Kalabai with his son Ambalal sitting as a pillion rider was going to her resident from their side.

At that time near Mangodh square a motorcycle bearing registration No.M.P. 11 MZ 6769 came reashly and negligently and collided with their motorcylce as a result of which Kalabai fell down and received head injuries.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8398 2 MA-7644-2023 She was admitted in the hospital but eventually died during treatment.
The offence was registered at Crime No.544/2020.

3. The claims tribunal after recording the evidence, considering the documents of the criminal case as well as other testimonies concluded that the accident was caused by the offending vehicle due to its rash and negligent driving by the driver and consequently, the compensation was awarded to the tune of Rs.11,71,000/- to the claimants.
4. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the amount of compensation is inadequate.

Learned counsel for the appellant(s) submits that the income of the deceased has been assessed as Rs.7000/- per month which is on the lower side, whereas as per the circular issued under the Ambalal vs Mukesh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13971667/
1 Minimum Wages Act by the Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh, the income of an unskilled labour on the date of incident is Rs.8400/-.

entities.text: Labour Department of State of Madhya Pradesh
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
Learned counsel also submits that the Claims Tribunal has assessed the future prospects of the deceased at 25% only whereas it should be 40%
when indisputably the age of the deceased at the time of incident is below 40 years since there is no evidence that deceased was above 40 years on record.

5 . Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has opposed the prayer on the ground that learned Claims Tribunal has taken due care of all the parameters for assessing just and proper compensation, therefore, no interference is required by allowing this appeal, hence prays for dismissal of the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8398 3 MA-7644-2023 6.
Heard and considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7. In light of the aforesaid, where the income of the deceased is taken on guess work, Circular issued under the Minimum Wages Act should be resorted to.

Accordingly, on the date of accident i.e. on 24.11.2020 income of the deceased is to be taken as Rs.8400/- per month considering her as 'Unskilled Labour' and for this, judgment passed by the Apex Court in Chandra @ Chanda @
Chandraram & Anr. vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav , (2022) 1 SCC 198 shall be referred.

entities.text:
Chandra @ Chanda @
Chandraram & Anr. vs. Mukesh Kumar Yadav , (2022) 1 SCC 198
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the head of future prospects, 40% is to be added as per directions given in para 59.3 & 59.4 of the judgment passed in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra) and multiplier of 15 has already been properly applied.

Accordingly, the just and proper compensation comes as under:-
Loss of dependency Rs.14,11,200/- (Rs.8400 +40% FP - 1/3rd x 12 x 15) Filial Consortium Rs.88,000/-
 Loss of Estate Rs.16,500/-
 Funeral expenses Rs.16,500/-
 Total Rs.15,32,200/-
 MACT Award Rs.11,71,000/-
 Enhanced Amount Rs.3,61,200/-
8.

Thus, in terms of the above modification, the appellants/claimants are entitled to receive the additional amount of compensation of Rs.3,61,200/- (enhanced amount of Rs.15,32,200 - Rs.11,71,000/- amount awarded by claims tribunal) over and above the amount which has been awarded by the claims Tribunal with the same rate of interest as awarded by NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8398 4 MA-7644-2023 the claims tribunal.

9. The appeal is valued as Rs.3,50,000/- and for the rest of the amount, the claimant(s) will pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days from today Ambalal vs Mukesh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13971667/
2 and only thereafter enhanced amount will be disbursed.
In case the appellant(s) fails to pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days then beyond 30 days interest will not be payable till filing of the Court fees.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award shall remain intact.
10. Accordingly, the appeal stands partly allowed and disposed off in above terms.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
Ambalal vs Mukesh on 31 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/13971667/
